BiblicalUsage: Hadad was a son of Ishmael, named in the list of his twelve sons. The King James spells his name Hadar in Genesis and Hadad in Chronicles, but the Hebrew is the same man.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two spellings are a small reminder to read carefully — one man, two spellings, and the same God keeping the list.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
